Description: The Localizer is a utility class that stores localized bundles, resolves the active localization from the current language, receives application configuration changes on a BroadcastChannel, and emits an event when the language changes. It is an EventTarget-based add-on rather than a custom element: it declares no Composition or Tag, and its gestures are named after the channel event it listens to (`message`) and the application configuration change that message carries (`onappconfigchange`) rather than after a user interaction.

localizations.description: A record of language codes mapped to localization bundles. Keys are language codes; values are localization bundles or undefined. Supplied once through the constructor and internally owned thereafter.

language.description: The active language used to resolve the current lexicon. The constructor seeds it, in order, from `options.language`, then the language persisted at `localStorage[options.storage]` when `storage` is configured and holds a non-empty value (storage that cannot be read counts as empty), then `navigator.language`; the seed is normalized (`en-US` becomes `en`). Constructor options are an object with optional string fields `language` and `storage`, read once at construction and not kept; any other options value, including a bare string, throws `Invalid options value: <value>`, and a present non-string field throws `Invalid options value: <field> is invalid`. Storage is never written. Seeding does not emit an event. Later assignments through `language` or `setLanguage()` are stored verbatim. Falsy assignments are ignored; non-string assignments throw `Invalid language value: <value>`. Setting the same value does not emit an event.
language.default: <options.language, else the persisted language at options.storage, else navigator.language — normalized to base lowercase language code>

lexicon.description: The resolved localization bundle for the current language. Resolution order: the bundle matching `language`, then the English bundle `en`, then the first available bundle. Throws `Localizer: no localization bundles are available.` when none exists.

initialize.description: Opens a BroadcastChannel on `Channels.configuration` and listens for its `message` events. Idempotent: calling it while already initialized opens no second channel and registers no second listener.

dispose.description: Removes the `message` listener registered by `initialize()` and closes the Localizer's BroadcastChannel. Listeners on the Localizer itself, such as `onlanguagechange`, are kept. Idempotent: calling it while not initialized has no effect.

setLanguage.description: Updates the active language by delegating to the `language` setter.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: The new language value to store. Falsy values are ignored.

onlanguagechange.description: Triggered when the active language changes to a new truthy value. Not triggered when the assigned language is falsy or equals the current language.

configuration.name: app.configuration
configuration.description: The BroadcastChannel on which application configuration changes are announced. The channel is shared: other senders post on it and messages may carry fields the Localizer does not read. A BroadcastChannel reaches every same-origin context, so a change announced in one tab reaches the Localizers in every open tab. The Localizer opens its own instance in `initialize()` and closes it in `dispose()`; it never posts on the channel.

message.description: A configuration message on the channel, as far as the Localizer reads it. Other fields may be present and are ignored. This describes what the Localizer accepts, not the full application message senders build; that belongs in the application's contract.

type.description: Identifies the message as an application configuration change.

language.description: Optional new language. Only a non-empty string is used.

onappconfigchange.description: An application configuration change, announced as a `Configuration` message on `Channels.configuration` whose `data.type` is `onappconfigchange`. The channel carries more than language changes, so a message is never an error for the Localizer: data that is not an object, an array, another `type`, a message without `language` (for example coding only), or a `language` that is not a non-empty string is ignored silently — `language` is unchanged, `onlanguagechange` is not emitted, and nothing is thrown. Extra fields on an accepted message are ignored.

triggers.condition: data is a Configuration message with a non-empty string language (Validate.configuration) — assigns `language` directly

message.description: The BroadcastChannel `message` event on `Channels.configuration`. Observed only after `initialize()` has been called and until `dispose()`.

triggers.condition: on Channels.configuration, after initialize() — handled as onappconfigchange
